classification.difficultyReason: Convert ten years to months before substitution, round to whole rabbits and connect the resulting population growth with finite island resources to justify the long-term limitation.

content.prompt: The population of rabbits on an island is currently increasing according to the formula $N=300e^{0.15t}$, where $t$ is in months. Find the initial population and the population after 10 years, rounding to the nearest rabbit. Then decide whether this is a realistic model for the population of rabbits long-term, giving a reason.

answer.short: Initial population $300$ rabbits; after 10 years about $19\,697\,990\,741$ rabbits. Not realistic: exponential growth cannot continue forever.
answer.worked:
At $t=0$:
$$\begin{align*}N&=300e^{0.15(0)}\\N&=300\end{align*}$$
$10$ years $=120$ months.
$$\begin{align*}N&=300e^{0.15(120)}\\N&=300e^{18}\\N&\approx19\,697\,990\,741\end{align*}$$
No. The model predicts unlimited exponential growth, but limited food, space and other resources prevent a rabbit population from growing at this rate forever.
